subject: SpectraCare pilot: unit economics validation, MAP gating & eval checklist

Subject: Pilot MAP + cost assumptions — need unit econ sanity check

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our execs want a short mutual action plan (MAP) that explicitly captures the unit economics we used to size the pilot — tokens/$, expected cache hit rates, batching assumptions, and what would trigger a different pricing band. Procurement asked us to validate these numbers before we proceed to legal procurement.

I've attached a first-pass MAP from our side (SpectraCare_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a traffic sample. Can you: 1) confirm whether your tokens-per-second and batching assumptions match the pilot profile, 2) flag any assumptions that would materially change cost, and 3) note gating criteria for the evaluation (e.g., 95th pct latency, tokens/dollar thresholds)?

We need this for our budget committee on Wednesday. Simple table + short notes will do.

Best,

ava.brooks@spectracare.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: Pilot MAP + cost assumptions — need unit econ sanity check

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the MAP. Attaching an internal cost model and a short MAP template that calls out the gating metrics and the tokens/$ sensitivity bands. High level notes below, then Ben and Karthik will chime in with ops plumbing assumptions.

Quick take (short):
- Baseline tokens/$ in the MAP assumes average generation of 150 tokens per session with 20% of sessions requiring a 2nd turn. That maps to ~180 tokens/session.
- Default cache hit rate used: 12% prefix cache (session reuse) + 5% static prompt cache = ~17% overall. If you can increase prefix reuse to 25% (small UX change), unit cost drops ~14%.
- Batching: we modeled conservative batching with 40ms scheduling window and target batch sizes of 8 for peak; effective tokens/sec improves ~1.6x over naive per-request. If your traffic is very bursty (spikes > 250 rps), we recommend a 20ms window and dynamic batching which increases throughput but raises 95th pct latency slightly.
- Gating criteria for evaluation: 95th pct end-to-end latency < 700ms, tokens/$ below $0.0035 at pilot scale (50k sessions/day), and no higher-than-expected degradation of generation quality on sample evals.

I've attached: spectracare_token_model.csv (detailed per-route tokens, hit-rate sensitivity) and SpectraCare_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP template + timeline). Next steps: 1) Ben to confirm batching numbers and threshold tradeoffs; 2) Karthik to confirm KV/prefetch assumptions and quantization impact on cost/latency; 3) we sync Wed EOD and finalize for your budget committee.

Thanks — Vivek
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Pilot MAP + cost assumptions — need unit econ sanity check

Ava — quick batch/cost notes and a small ask on traffic profiling.

1) Batching windows: our conservative model (40ms window) assumes median inter-arrival times that match your sample. In practice we see best throughput/latency tradeoffs with an adaptive window: 20ms during peak, 60ms during off-peak. For the pilot, if you can provide a 24-hr RPS histogram split by production vs. test (CSV), we will tune the window to hit your latency SLO while maximizing batch size.

2) Token accounting: the attached CSV splits tokens into prompt vs. generated tokens per route. Pricing sensitivity: moving from int8 to int4 quantization reduces token cost by ~18% in our model but may add ~10-30ms tail latency depending on model. We only recommend int4 for routes that are tolerant of that tail shift.

3) Cache/prefetch: the 'prefetching-assumptions.pdf' attached outlines two approaches: (A) prefix reuse (client-side cookie/session keys), (B) server-side proactive prefetch for common starting prompts. The latter improves apparent hit-rate early in sessions but increases ops complexity. If SpectraCare can enable client-side session identifiers, we expect to hit the 25% prefix reuse number Vivek mentioned.

Ask: can procurement share the expected peak RPS and % of multi-turn flows? That will materially change the tokens/day and the pilot pricing band.

—Ben
Principal Product Manager, Performance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Brooks <ava.brooks@spectracare.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Pilot MAP + cost assumptions — need unit econ sanity check

Hi all — technical guardrails and items that affect unit economics:

- KV cache: for multi-turn flows we assume KV cache hit of 70% on repeated tokens within the same session; cross-session KV sharing is disabled for PHI-sensitive prompts unless explicitly allowed. If SpectraCare opts into cross-session KV for non-PHI prompts, you'll see another ~8-12% cost reduction.

- Quantization: Ben called out int4 vs int8; we also must consider model variant — smaller context/shorter sequence variants (e.g., 2k vs 8k context) reduce per-token runtime memory overhead and lower latency. For evaluation, we propose running the quality baseline on both int8 and int4 for the top 5 failing prompts to confirm no regressions.

- Prefetch: server-side prefetch gives better early-session hit-rate but increases peak GPU memory pressure by ~6-9%. We'll include a stress test in the evaluation plan.

I added a short ops checklist in the MAP spreadsheet: what we need from SpectraCare for canonical runs (RPS histogram, sample sessions labeled multi-turn, flagged PHI vs non-PHI). With those we can populate the tokens/day and tokens/$ buckets precisely.

—Karthik
Senior SW Eng, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
